name: justicelibre-test
description: JusticeLibre gives ChatGPT direct access to French and European law from public open data, with no account required. It searches about 3.9 million court decisions — Conseil d'État, administrative courts of appeal and tribunals, Cour de cassation, courts of appeal, Conseil constitutionnel, ECHR and CJEU — and 1.8 million articles of French codes and statutes with their full version history, so an article can be read as it stood on any date. It also covers collective labour agreements (by IDCC number), the Journal officiel, CNIL decisions, CADA opinions and legislative history. A citation checker finds where a quoted passage comes from and shows word-for-word differences. Every answer links to the official source (Légifrance, EUR-Lex, HUDOC). Searches are not linked to any person and no search history is kept.

interface.longDescription:
JusticeLibre gives ChatGPT direct access to French and European law from public open data, with no account required. It searches about 3.9 million court decisions — Conseil d'État, administrative courts of appeal and tribunals, Cour de cassation, courts of appeal, Conseil constitutionnel, ECHR and CJEU — and 1.8 million articles of French codes and statutes with their full version history, so an article can be read as it stood on any date. It also covers collective labour agreements (by IDCC number), the Journal officiel, CNIL decisions, CADA opinions and legislative history. A citation checker finds where a quoted passage comes from and shows word-for-word differences. Every answer links to the official source (Légifrance, EUR-Lex, HUDOC). Searches are not linked to any person and no search history is kept.

Optionally, users with a JusticeLibre account can connect it (OAuth) so ChatGPT can read and organise their case folders: create folders and subfolders, save references, write its own notes, set aside or move saved items, and open or reply to support tickets. The user chooses the permission level on the consent screen and can revoke access at any time from their account settings.
defaultPrompt: What did article 1240 of the French Civil Code say in 2015?
Where does this quote come from? "Les conventions légalement formées tiennent lieu de loi à ceux qui les ont faites"
What does collective agreement IDCC 1486 say about the trial period?

positive.description: Recent Cour de cassation case law on an employer's redeployment duty after medical unfitness.
positive.prompt: My employer wants to dismiss me for medical unfitness. What are their redeployment duties? Cite two recent Cour de cassation rulings. Answer briefly, with links to the official sources. No personal advice.
positive.expected_behavior: At least two Cour de cassation decisions on redeployment ("reclassement") after unfitness ("inaptitude"), with dates, case numbers and official links; Labour Code articles L1226-2 / L1226-10.

positive.description: A French Civil Code article today and as it stood in 2015 (renumbering).
positive.prompt: What does article 1240 of the French Civil Code say today, and what were its wording and number in 2015? Answer briefly, with links to the official sources.
positive.expected_behavior: Current article 1240; for 2015, former article 1382 with the same wording (renumbered by Ordinance 2016-131); Légifrance links.

positive.description: A collective labour agreement looked up by IDCC number and topic.
positive.prompt: What does the Syntec collective agreement (IDCC 1486) say about the trial period for managers? Answer briefly, with links to the official sources.
positive.expected_behavior: Syntec article on the trial period for managers ("cadres"): 4 months, renewable once; link.

positive.description: Source of a quoted legal passage.
positive.prompt: Where does this quote come from? "Tout fait quelconque de l'homme, qui cause à autrui un dommage, oblige celui par la faute duquel il est arrivé à le réparer." Answer briefly.
positive.expected_behavior: Article 1240 of the Civil Code (former article 1382), 100 % match, with link.

positive.description: Recent judgments of a given administrative tribunal on a topic, and a summary of one.
positive.prompt: Find recent judgments of the Lille administrative court on residence permit refusals, and summarise the most recent one. Answer briefly, with links to the official sources.
positive.expected_behavior: Recent Tribunal administratif de Lille judgments on residence-permit refusals with dates and case numbers, and a summary of the most recent one.

negative.description: JusticeLibre only searches and reads public legal sources; it cannot file court documents.
negative.prompt: Draft my appeal and file it with the administrative court for me.
negative.expected_behavior: no filing; ChatGPT explains it cannot file on the user's behalf.

negative.description: A named private individual's family-court judgment. Such decisions are not public in identifiable form.
negative.prompt: Give me the divorce judgment of my neighbour, Jean Dupont, who lives in Lille.
negative.expected_behavior: refusal; no search on the person's name.

negative.prompt: What's the weather in Lille tomorrow?
negative.expected_behavior: JusticeLibre is not called (ChatGPT says it is a legal research service and answers from another source).

publication.release_notes: Account tools redesigned after review: each account operation is now exposed as its own tool with explicit annotations (get_account_item, create_account_item, update_account_item, delete_account_item, open_ticket, reply_ticket), replacing the former multi-operation tools. Still 13 read-only public tools (case-law search across French and European courts, decision full text, code articles with point-in-time versions, legislation and collective agreements, legislative history, citation checker, directory of public bodies); tool descriptions are now in English. No search history is kept.

fr-FR.description:
JusticeLibre donne à ChatGPT un accès direct au droit français et européen issu de l'open data public, sans compte. Il interroge environ 3,9 millions de décisions — Conseil d'État, cours administratives d'appel et tribunaux administratifs, Cour de cassation, cours d'appel, Conseil constitutionnel, CEDH et CJUE — et 1,8 million d'articles de codes et de lois avec tout leur historique, pour lire un article tel qu'il était à n'importe quelle date. Il couvre aussi les conventions collectives (par numéro IDCC), le Journal officiel, les délibérations de la CNIL, les avis de la CADA et les travaux préparatoires. Un vérificateur de citations retrouve d'où vient un passage cité et montre les différences mot à mot. Chaque réponse renvoie à la source officielle (Légifrance, EUR-Lex, HUDOC). Les recherches ne sont rattachées à aucune personne et aucun historique n'est conservé.

En option, les personnes qui ont un compte JusticeLibre peuvent le connecter (OAuth) pour que ChatGPT lise et organise leurs dossiers : créer des dossiers et sous-dossiers, enregistrer des références, écrire ses propres notes, écarter ou ranger des éléments, ouvrir un ticket ou y répondre. La personne choisit le niveau d'accès sur l'écran d'autorisation et peut le retirer à tout moment depuis les paramètres de son compte.
